overview.text: NNPC, Nigeria's state oil company, is considering a Lagos initial public offering that could float up to a 10% stake, its CEO told Reuters.
The federal government says it will recover N400 billion in unpaid charges and pledges to tackle power shortages.
Stakeholders called for a forensic audit of NIMASA vessel funds.
The UK and Nigeria moved to mobilise private capital for three hydropower projects, per a Punch headline.
Zamfara Governor Dauda Lawal approved recruitment of technical staff for the state's Internal Revenue Service.

cards.headline: Nigeria’s state oil company mulls IPO
cards.what_happened: NNPC, Nigeria's state oil company, is considering an initial public offering in Lagos that could float up to a 10% stake. Its CEO told Reuters the company may follow the listing with a secondary listing in London or New York. The article text is truncated, so further details on timing and structure are not available.
key_facts: NNPC could float up to a 10% stake in a Lagos initial public offering.
NNPC's CEO told Reuters the listing could be followed by a secondary listing in London or New York.
analysis: Why it matters: A partial public listing of the state oil company would bring its ownership and governance under public-market disclosure rules, which bears on transparency over public assets.

cards.headline: Stakeholders call for forensic audit of NIMASA vessel funds
cards.what_happened: Stakeholders have called for a forensic audit of funds linked to vessels under the Nigerian Maritime Administration and Safety Agency (NIMASA). The article text provided is limited to the headline, so the scope of the funds and the basis for the call are not detailed.
key_facts: Stakeholders called for a forensic audit of NIMASA vessel funds.

cards.headline: UK, Nigeria mobilise private capital for three hydro projects
cards.what_happened: The United Kingdom and Nigeria have moved to mobilise private capital for three hydropower projects, according to a Punch Newspapers headline. The available text contains no further detail on the investors, amounts or project locations.
analysis: Why it matters: Private capital mobilisation for public infrastructure can involve new corporate counterparties and ownership arrangements, but the article text provided does not give enough detail to assess this.

cards.headline: Edo State Electricity Market Under Threat As Chinese Firm, CCETC, Continues To Disobey Nigerian Court Orders – Ossiomo Power Company
cards.what_happened: Ossiomo Power Company has accused Chinese firm CCETC of continuing to disobey Nigerian court orders, a dispute it says threatens the electricity market in Edo State.
key_facts: Ossiomo Power Company says CCETC continues to disobey Nigerian court orders.
analysis: As reported by independentng; AURA has not checked court or agency records. An allegation or charge is not a finding of guilt.
